    AI Overview
    Yes, the Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team has won
    one NCAA National Championship in its history    , defeating Seton Hall 80-79 in overtime to win the 1989 NCAA Tournament under interim head coach Steve Fisher. 
    Key facts about Michigan’s tournament history include: 
    • 1989 Champions: Led by tournament MVP Glen Rice, who set the record for most points in a single NCAA tournament.
    • Final Four History: Michigan has appeared in the Final Four nine times (1964, 1965, 1976, 1989, 1992, 1993, 2013, 2018, 2026).
    • Championship Game Record: The team is 1-6 all-time in national championship games, with losses in 1965, 1976, 1992, 1993, 2013, and 2018.
    • Vacated Appearances: Due to NCAA sanctions, the program vacated its 1992 and 1993 Final Four appearances. 
    (Note: As of April 2026, Michigan is currently scheduled to play in the NCAA championship game, as mentioned in the search results, but the 1989 title remains their only official championship prior to that game)..

    AI Overview
    The Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team has won
    one NCAA national championship in its program history, achieved in 1989 under interim head coach Steve Fisher. The team has finished as the national runner-up six times (1964, 1965, 1976, 1992, 1993, 2013, 2018), with the 1992 and 1993 appearances later vacated. 
    Key details: 
    • Championship Year: 1989 (defeated Seton Hall 80-79 in OT).
    • Final Four Appearances: 8 (1964, 1965, 1976, 1989, 1992*, 1993*, 2013, 2018).
    • Conference Titles: 16 Big Ten Regular Season Titles. 
    *Note: The 1992 and 1993 Final Four appearances and additional wins were vacated due to NCAA violations
    .
